newsitem.title: USA: LSI, Micron in specialized computer chip venture.
newsitem.headline: LSI, Micron in specialized computer chip venture.

text.p: LSI Logic Corp and Micron Technology Inc have agreed to jointly develop and manufacture specialized microprocessors for a variety of consumer electronics, the companies said Monday.
The companies will design a logic chip that includes embedded memory, a design that will replace several chips with a single one, reducing manufacturing costs, officials of both companies said.

"This could be a $3 billion to $5 billion market in three to five years," said Steve Appleton, Micron chairman and chief executive. "You would be surprised how much development is going on" by chip companies.

Currently, the logic chips that control the basic functions of consumers electronics -- everything from toys to stereos to cameras -- do not have memory. Manufacturers have to buy and install separate memory chips in their products, increasing material costs and manufacturing expense.

LSI, which specializes in making custom logic chips, and Micron, which specializes in memory chips, will combine their expertise to design these chips. Each company will fund its own research, the companies said.
Depending on the customer and size of the order, the chips will be made either in LSI's Gresham, Oregon, chip factory, or Micron's Boise, Idaho, facility, the companies said.
Initial chips are expected to be developed by the middle of 1998. The companies will split revenues for each order, said Wilfred Corrigan, LSI's chairman and chief executive.
